name: Ephedrine/caffeine (ECA stack)
lead: The ECA stack is a combination of ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin used as a fat-loss and energy aid, particularly in bodybuilding and physique-cutting circles. Ephedrine is a sympathomimetic stimulant derived from or chemically identical to the alkaloids of the ephedra plant, and caffeine is thought to amplify its effects.[1]

A 2021 systematic review summarized on Wikipedia reported that ephedrine, with or without caffeine, taken for roughly 4 to 24 weeks was associated with about 2 kg more weight loss than placebo, with no statistically significant blood pressure difference in that review.[1] Ephedrine is also associated with insomnia, anxiety, raised blood pressure, fast heart rate, and, in serious cases, stroke and heart attack.[1]

In the United States, the FDA banned ephedrine-alkaloid dietary supplements marketed for purposes other than traditional uses in 2004, and a federal appeals court upheld that rule in 2006.[1] Users on looksmax.org have written ECA guides that frame it as a cutting aid to be paired with exercise and caution against it for people with heart problems.[2]
infobox: Ephedrine-alkaloid supplements banned by FDA (2004, upheld 2006)[1]

paras: ECA stands for ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin. Community guides describe it as a stack for raising metabolism, suppressing appetite and boosting energy during dieting.[2] Wikipedia describes the stack as popular among bodybuilders who aim to reduce body fat before competitions.[1]

Ephedrine alone is described as producing modest short-term weight loss, mainly fat, with unknown long-term effects. Caffeine and other methylxanthines have been reported to act synergistically with ephedrine, which led to combination products.[1] A 2021 systematic review reported around 2 kg more weight loss than placebo at the doses and durations studied.[1]

Reported effects of ephedrine include insomnia, anxiety, headache, hallucinations, high blood pressure, fast heart rate, reduced appetite and urinary retention. Stroke and heart attack have been reported as serious events.[1] By 2004 the FDA had received more than 18,000 adverse-event reports linked to ephedrine products.[1] The looksmax.org guide itself states that the stack should not be used by people with heart problems.[2]

Ephedra (ma huang) has been documented in Chinese medicine since the Han dynasty. Ephedrine was first synthesized in 1885 by Nagai Nagayoshi, and Merck marketed it in the 1920s.[1] The FDA proposed dose limits in 1997, banned ephedrine-alkaloid supplements in 2004, and the Tenth Circuit upheld the ban in August 2006.[1] Health Canada issued a voluntary recall in January 2002 of products above 8 mg per dose, those combined with other stimulants such as caffeine, and those marketed for weight loss or bodybuilding.[1] Ephedrine is banned by several sports bodies including the NCAA, MLB, NFL and PGA.[1] Availability varies by country.[2]

The Wikipedia summary cites a 2021 systematic review of ephedrine, with or without caffeine, reporting about 2 kg additional weight loss versus placebo over 4 to 24 weeks.[1] No studies specific to appearance outcomes in lean, physique-focused users were found.

timeline.event: Ephedrine first synthesized by Nagai Nagayoshi.[1]
Ephedrine introduced for medical use in the US.[1]
Health Canada voluntary recall of high-dose and combination ephedrine products.[1]
Tenth Circuit upholds the FDA rule.[1]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the stack is discussed in a how-to guide aimed at fat loss while cutting.[2]

claims.claim: ECA raises metabolism and suppresses appetite for fat loss
claims.believers: The guide author describes it as a stack for metabolism, appetite suppression and energy that assists weight-loss efforts.[2]
claims.experts: A 2021 systematic review summarized on Wikipedia found about 2 kg more weight loss than placebo over 4 to 24 weeks.[1]

claims.claim: It is only worthwhile alongside exercise
claims.believers: The guide says using it without exercising is pointless and compares it to taking a painkiller without pain.[2]
claims.experts: No published studies were found that test this specific claim.

claims.claim: It is safe if you have no heart problems
claims.believers: The guide warns against use with heart conditions and implies healthy users are acceptable.[2]
claims.experts: Reported effects include raised blood pressure, fast heart rate, stroke and heart attack, and the FDA banned ephedrine-alkaloid supplements in 2004.[1]

card.summary: A classic ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin cutting stack with modest reported fat-loss effects and a long regulatory history.
card.note: Ephedrine-alkaloid supplements are banned in the US; cardiovascular events have been reported.

quick.overview:
ECA combines ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin. It is used in bodybuilding and physique communities as a cutting aid for appetite suppression and energy.

A 2021 systematic review summarized on Wikipedia reported about 2 kg more weight loss than placebo over 4 to 24 weeks.
quick.mechanism: Ephedrine is a sympathomimetic stimulant; caffeine has been reported to act synergistically with it.
quick.risks: Reported effects include insomnia, anxiety, high blood pressure, fast heart rate, stroke and heart attack. The FDA banned ephedrine-alkaloid supplements in 2004; legal status varies elsewhere.
